summary: test52 is a 26,871-variable/53,467-row five-weight selection model: 266 blocks of 50 scores, one cover row and four comparison rows each. The committed target (1,271 vars/2,326 rows) drops 51,141 rows and 25,600 variables by strict-dominance fixings, threshold substitution and exact big-M tightening. The kernel certificate is 3 claims / 368,611 top-level steps / 238,241 obligations / 78,134,488 bytes, verified in 14.4 s at work 14,598,974 and peak_live_facts 151,543. The 29-turn corpus-maximum blind analysis re-derived the same block fact base in about four passes; the 313-line shared preparer then re-derived it again and hand-assembled the entire rule family from Lin/EqPair/Cases primitives.
claims: 3 claims = {forward,reverse} x {integer,LP}: source 26,871 vars/53,467 rows to target 1,271/2,326, objective Equal, inverse 0/1/None (cases/test52/request.json); obligations 33,850/109,481/94,910 = 238,241.

The 1,271-pair projection maps target variables onto their original source indices; the reverse map reconstructs 13,300 score variables and 55 eliminated thresholds as exact affine forms in the five weights, not just coordinate identities.

12,190 binaries are fixed to zero by a strictly smaller score in every weight coordinate (positive minimum delta), 55 to one by U=0 or a single surviving candidate; ties stay legal because Cases asks whether y_z is selected, never one-hotness.
Four fixed-zero gap rows survive: their best surviving-candidate epsilon margins (59977/10000000000, 24997/5000000000, 80019/10000000000, 69961/10000000000) are all below epsilon=1/100000.
LP inclusion only in the third claim: target-LP inclusion into the source LP is proved, while LP equality and strictness are explicitly not claimed (cases/test52/preparation.json:29).
proof_encoding: 'RPA 2' plus one JSON object {claims:[3], blocks:[3]}; each block is {steps, end.Return{map, checks}}; only Lin, EqPair and Cases steps, with checks that are Exact, VarLower/VarUpper/VarInt refs or local Lin refs.

404,024 Lin, 30,479 Cases and 12,300 EqPair step records; verify reports branches 30479, obligations 238241, linear_terms 2812574, substitution_terms 887844, work 14598974, peak_live_facts 151543 (cases/test52/preparation.json:103).

The 1,055 tightened upper rows and 55 forced-one blocks are proved by a balanced-split Cases recursion over each block's surviving candidates: selected_bound() bisects the candidate list, assumes integer-ness of the left half, and nests Cases down to one candidate.

EqPair splits exactly: 12,190 zero certificates (assumption y_z=0 against the VarLower fact) + 55 forced-one + 55 threshold equalities; score definitions are canonical source equalities oriented variable-minus-reconstruction (tools/prepare_test51.py:78).
78,134,488 bytes (74.5 MB) assemble deterministically in 2.9 s to a 50,227,346-byte RPX; proof_max_depth 7, json_max_depth 33, and RPA/request stay well inside the 256 MiB text budget.
agent_manual_work: Wrote an exact MPS reader over fractions.Fraction of numeric lexemes (Fraction used 59 times; 52,009 characters of eval code across 22 eval calls) and a second fixed-field cross-check after the two failing calls.

Re-derived the decomposition repeatedly: shape_groups/triples/row_index in one cell, dominance witnesses plus all 13,300 difference bounds in another, then re-verified every witness and every bound from the original rows in the audit cell.

Invented the 10,843,990-byte audit.json schema (fixed_zero_binaries, deleted_gap_row_certificates, tightened_upper_rows, removed_rows_by_rule) that the kernel-side preparer now consumes as its certificate source.
Hand-wrote the target MPS with a decimal_exact writer plus an independent free-MPS reader, then audited all 2,326 rows by symbolic substitution back into the corresponding original rows.
Evaluated 26 predetermined rational weight points exactly (10 feasible, lifted exactly; 16 violating gap rows in both models) as the only non-RPA evidence of the reformulation.
preparer_helpers: structure(a) (tools/prepare_test51.py:31-69): asserts c0 is the 5-weight simplex and rebuilds definitions, scores, comparison quadruples and cover groups from canonical rows - the entire decomposition.

cases() (:17) plus Builder/SparseBuilder (tools/prepare_test88.py:18, tools/prepare_test70.py:14): the untrusted proof-state accumulator (alloc/lin/eqpair/refexpr/kind) that sibling preparers test21, test22, test46, test70, test78 and test87 redefine or subclass.
selected_bound() (:107) with source_score_bound() (:89) and vector_bound() (:80): the conditional big-M and selected-minimum proofs, including the Cases recursion and the epsilon witnesses.
reverse_checks(integer,inverse) (:206): one shared 238,241-obligation check list reused for both reverse claims, dispatching per row over comparison, cover and definition rows.
run_case() (:270) plus the 5-line tools/prepare_test52.py: subprocess harness, four negative mutations, deterministic re-assembly/re-verify and the preparation.json writer.
friction: Both failing calls share one cause: classic MPS fixed fields ([24:36]/[39:47]/[49:61]) against this file's widened records ([24:48]/[50:58]/[60:84]); the token parser was right, so three further cells went into measuring boundaries and re-running the 199,441-entry cross-check.
The block structure was re-derived or re-verified in roughly four of 22 eval cells, and the preparer's structure() derives it once more: 199,175 nonzeros scanned on each pass.

No kernel type defines the fixing/substitution/deletion records, so the analyst's audit.json is the only handoff, and its keys differ between test51 and test52 for identical concepts, forcing three 'if number==51' schema branches in the preparer.

inspect-model reports counts only {rows, variables, integers, nonzeros} and export-model gives terms as positional [index, coefficient] pairs, so both the analyst and the preparer build their own incidence indexes to find covers, quadruples and the simplex.

The boundary between certified and over-claimed deletion is invisible to the API: nothing checks that a deletion witness margin is at least epsilon, so the preparer re-derives that predicate itself (tools/prepare_test51.py:202).
